questions.stem: The JALLIANWALA BAGH massacre took place on:
questions.explanation: 13 April 1919 — Baisakhi day. General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, protesting the Rowlatt Act. Official British toll: 379; Indian estimates: 1,000+. Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The DANDI MARCH / SALT SATYAGRAHA was launched on:
questions.explanation: Gandhi started from Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) on 12 March 1930 with 78 followers. Walked 385 km to Dandi (Gujarat coast). Broke the salt law by making salt from seawater on 6 April 1930. Marked the start of Civil Disobedience Movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Match the MOVEMENT with its YEAR. A. Non-Cooperation Movement.  B. Civil Disobedience Movement.  C. Quit India Movement.  D. Champaran Satyagraha. List-II: 1. 1920.  2. 1930.  3. 1942.  4. 1917.
questions.explanation: 1917 — Champaran (Gandhi's first satyagraha in India — indigo cultivators). 1920 — Non-Cooperation (post-Jallianwala + Khilafat). 1930 — Civil Disobedience / Salt March. 1942 — Quit India ('Do or Die') launched from Bombay Session, 8 August 1942.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The CRIPPS MISSION came to India in:
questions.explanation: Sir Stafford Cripps came in March 1942 with British proposals for dominion status after WWII in exchange for Indian cooperation. Gandhi called it 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'. Failure led to the Quit India Movement in August.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged by the British on:
questions.explanation: 23 March 1931 — hanged at Lahore Central Jail in the Saunders murder case. 'Shaheed Diwas' observed on this date in their memory. Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed just weeks earlier (5 March 1931) — but did not include commutation.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The slogan 'DO OR DIE' was given during:
questions.explanation: 'Karenge ya Marenge' (Do or Die) — Gandhi's call at the Quit India session (Bombay, 8 August 1942). Congress Working Committee passed the Quit India Resolution. Most senior leaders were immediately arrested; student and underground leadership took over.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The LAHORE SESSION of Congress (1929) is famous for the resolution on:
questions.explanation: Lahore Session, December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru as Congress President. Adopted 'Purna Swaraj' resolution, set 26 January 1930 as Independence Day (which was celebrated annually till 1947). That date was later chosen as the day the Constitution came into force in 1950. complete independence.
